Method of Attack: Creates and hides scheduled tasks on compromised Windows systems by deleting the Security Descriptor registry value to conceal tasks from traditional identification methods
Maintains persistence by re-establishing dropped connections to command-and-control (C2) infrastructure
Uses a previously unknown Windows bug to hide scheduled tasks from 'schtasks /query' and Task Scheduler
Attack Vector: Use of Impacket tooling for lateral movement and execution
Indicators of Compromise: Scheduled tasks without an SD (security descriptor) value within their Task Key in Windows Registry
Events in Security.evtx and Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational.evtx logs related to hidden scheduled tasks
Outbound connections from critical Tier 0 and Tier 1 assets to command-and-control infrastructure
